Volume of parallelopiped $=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & \alpha & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & \alpha \\ \alpha & 0 & 1\end{array}\right|$
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}=1+\alpha^3-\alpha$
For maxima or minima,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{d} \alpha}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 \alpha^2-1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~d} \alpha^2}=6 \alpha$
For $\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$,
$\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~d} x^2}>0$
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}$ is minimum at $\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

question.text: If the volume of tetrahedron, whose vertices are with position vectors $\hat{i}-6 \hat{j}+10 \hat{k},-\hat{i}-3 \hat{j}+7 \hat{k}$, $5 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+\lambda \hat{k}$ and $7 \hat{i}-4 \hat{j}+7 \hat{k}$ is 11 cubic units, then value of $\lambda$ is

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } \overline{\mathrm{a}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}-6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+10 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \text {, } \\ & \overline{\mathrm{b}}=-\hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \text {, } \\ & \overline{\mathrm{c}}=5 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\lambda \hat{\mathrm{k}} \text {, } \\ & \overline{\mathrm{d}}=7 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+7 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \therefore \quad \overline{\mathrm{AB}}=-2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \overline{\mathrm{AC}}=4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+5 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+(\lambda-10) \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \overline{\mathrm{AD}}=6 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \therefore \quad \text { Volume of tetrahedron }=\frac{1}{6}\left[\begin{array}{lll}\overline{\mathrm{AB}} & \overline{\mathrm{AC}} & \overline{\mathrm{AD}}\end{array}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow 11=\frac{1}{6}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}-2 & 3 & -3 \\ 4 & 5 & \lambda-10 \\ 6 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right| \\ & \Rightarrow 11=\frac{1}{6}\{-2(-15-2 \lambda+20)-3(-12-6 \lambda+60) \\  & -3(8-30)\} \\ & \Rightarrow \lambda=7& \end{aligned}$

question.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ are any three non-zero vectors, then $(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}+\bar{c}) \cdot[(\bar{a}-\bar{b}) \times(\bar{a}-\bar{b}-\bar{c})]=$

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & (\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}+\bar{c}) \cdot[(\bar{a}-\bar{b}) \times(\bar{a}-\bar{b}-\bar{c})] \\ & =(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}+\bar{c}) \cdot(\bar{a} \times \bar{a}-\bar{a} \times \bar{b}-\bar{a} \times \bar{c}-\bar{b} \times \bar{a}+\bar{b} \times \bar{b}+\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) \\ & =(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}+\bar{c}) \cdot(\overline{0}-\bar{a} \times \bar{b}-\bar{a} \times \bar{c}+\bar{a} \times \bar{b}+\overline{0}+\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) \\ & =(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\ & =\bar{a} \cdot(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})+\bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})+2 \bar{b} \cdot(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})+2 \bar{b} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) \\ & +\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\ & =\overline{0}+\bar{a} \cdot(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})+2 \bar{b} \cdot(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})+2 \times 0-0-0 \\ & =\left[\begin{array}{lll}\overline{\mathrm{a}} & \overline{\mathrm{b}} & \overline{\mathrm{c}}\end{array}\right]+2\left[\begin{array}{lll}\overline{\mathrm{b}} & \overline{\mathrm{c}} & \overline{\mathrm{a}}\end{array}\right] \\ & =\left[\begin{array}{lll}\overline{\mathrm{a}} & \overline{\mathrm{b}} & \overline{\mathrm{c}}\end{array}\right]+2\left[\begin{array}{lll}\overline{\mathrm{a}} & \overline{\mathrm{b}} & \overline{\mathrm{c}}\end{array}\right] \\ & =3\left[\begin{array}{lll}\overline{\mathrm{a}} & \overline{\mathrm{b}} & \overline{\mathrm{c}}\end{array}\right] \\ & \end{aligned}$

question.text: The volume of parallelopiped, whose coterminous edges are given by $\bar{u}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\lambda \hat{k}$, $\bar{v}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}, \bar{w}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ is 1 cu. units. If $\theta$ is the angle between $\bar{u}$ and $\bar{w}$, then the value of $\cos \theta$ is

question.text: If $[(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{c}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{a}})] \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{c}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}})=54$, then the value of $\left[\begin{array}{lll}\bar{a} & \bar{b} & \bar{c}\end{array}\right]$ is

solution.text:
R.H.S. of the given equality can be written as
$\begin{aligned}
&(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot[(\overline{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \times(3 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+\overline{\mathrm{b}}+2 \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&=(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}) \cdot[3(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&+6(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+4(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&+9(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{a}})+3(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+6(\overline{\mathrm{c}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&=(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}})[0+(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+2(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&-6(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})+0+4(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}) \\
&=(2 \overline{\mathrm{a}}+3 \overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}})[-5(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})-3(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})+(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})-7(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&=-10[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})]+2[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]-14[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&-15[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})]+3[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]-21[\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&-5[\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})]+[\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})]-7[\overline{\mathrm{c}} \cdot(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})] \\
&= 0+2[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]+0 \\
&+0+0 \\
&=-5[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]+0+21[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}] \\
&= 18[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}} \overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]=54
\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow[\overline{\mathrm{a}} \overline{\mathrm{b}} \overline{\mathrm{c}}]=3$

question.text: The scalar product of the vector $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ with a unit vector along the sum of the vectors $2 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}-5 \hat{k}$ and $\lambda \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$ is equal to 1 , then value of $\lambda$ is

solution.text:
$(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}})+(\lambda \hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}})=(2+\lambda) \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$
Unit vector along the above vector is
$\frac{(2+\lambda) \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{(2+\lambda)^2+6^2+(-2)^2}}=\frac{(2+\lambda) \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}}$
Scalar product of $(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})$ with this unit vector is 1 .
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad & (\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \cdot \frac{(2+\lambda) \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}}=1 \\
& \frac{(2+\lambda)+6-2}{\sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}}=1 \\
& \sqrt{\lambda^2+4 \lambda+44}=\lambda+6 \\
\therefore \quad & \lambda^2+4 \lambda+44=(\lambda+6)^2 \\
& 8 \lambda=8 \\
& \lambda=1
\end{aligned}$

question.text: The value of $\alpha$, so that the volume of the parallelopiped formed by $\hat{i}+\alpha \hat{j}+\hat{k}, \hat{j}+\alpha \hat{k}$ and $\alpha \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ becomes maximum, is

solution.text:
Volume of parallelopiped is $[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}]$
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad V & =\left|\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & \alpha & 1 \\
0 & 1 & \alpha \\
\alpha & 0 & 1
\end{array}\right| \\
& =1-\alpha\left(-\alpha^2\right)-\alpha \\
& =1+\alpha^3-\alpha
\end{aligned}$
Differentiating w.r.t. $\alpha$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{d} \alpha}=3 \alpha^2-1 \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~d} \alpha^2}=6 \alpha \\
& \text { Let } \frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{d} \alpha}=0 \\
\therefore \quad & 3 \alpha^2-1=0 \\
\therefore \quad & \alpha= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\
& \text { at } \alpha=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}, \\

Given vectors $\bar{a} \& \bar{b}$ are unit vectors.
$\begin{array}{l}
\text { Now }(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b})] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b}) \times(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot[\bar{a} \times(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})+2 \bar{b} \times(\bar{a} \times \bar{b})] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})[(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{a}-(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a}) \cdot \bar{b}+2(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{a}-2(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{a}) \cdot \bar{b}] \\
\quad=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})[(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) \bar{a}-\bar{b}+2 \bar{a}-2(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{a}) \bar{b}] \\
\text { Here } \quad \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}=\frac{3(2)}{7 \sqrt{10}}-\frac{1(6)}{7 \sqrt{10}}=0
\end{array}$
Hence given expression becomes
$\begin{array}{l}
=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})[-\bar{b}+2 \bar{a}]=-(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b})^{2} \\
=-\left[4 \bar{a}^{2}+\bar{b}^{2}-4 \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}\right]=-(4+1)=-5
\end{array}$

question.text: If $\bar{p}, \bar{q}, \bar{r}$ are unit vectors such that $\bar{p} \times (\bar{q} \times \bar{r}) = \dfrac{1}{7}\bar{q}$, then the angle between $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{r}$ is

solution.text:
Using the vector triple product expansion:

$\bar{p} \times (\bar{q} \times \bar{r}) = (\bar{p} \cdot \bar{r})\bar{q} - (\bar{p} \cdot \bar{q})\bar{r}$

Given that $\bar{p} \times (\bar{q} \times \bar{r}) = \dfrac{1}{7}\bar{q}$, we have:

$(\bar{p} \cdot \bar{r})\bar{q} - (\bar{p} \cdot \bar{q})\bar{r} = \dfrac{1}{7}\bar{q}$

Since $\bar{q}$ is a unit vector, $\bar{q} \neq \bar{0}$. If $\bar{q}$ and $\bar{r}$ were collinear, $\bar{q} \times \bar{r} = \bar{0}$, which would imply $\dfrac{1}{7}\bar{q} = \bar{0}$, a contradiction. Thus, $\bar{q}$ and $\bar{r}$ are non-collinear vectors.

Equating the coefficients of $\bar{q}$ and $\bar{r}$ on both sides:

$\bar{p} \cdot \bar{r} = \dfrac{1}{7}$

$\bar{p} \cdot \bar{q} = 0$

Let $\theta$ be the angle between the unit vectors $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{r}$. Then:

$|\bar{p}| |\bar{r}| \cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{7}$

$\cos\theta = \dfrac{1}{7}$

Using the identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$:

$\sin\theta = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2\theta} = \sqrt{1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)^2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{48}{49}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3}}{7}$

$\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{3}}{7}\right)$

Answer: $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{3}}{7}\right)$

question.text: If $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are three non-coplanar vectors and $\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{r}$ are defined as $\vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{b} \times \vec{c}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}, \vec{q} = \dfrac{\vec{c} \times \vec{a}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}, \vec{r} = \dfrac{\vec{a} \times \vec{b}}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}$, then $[(\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{p} + (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{q} + (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{r}]$ is equal to

solution.text:
The given vectors $\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{r}$ are the reciprocal vectors of $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$.

Using the properties of reciprocal vectors, we have:
$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = \dfrac{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = 1$
$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{p} = \dfrac{\vec{b} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = 0$

Similarly, for the other dot products:
$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{q} = 1$, $\vec{c} \cdot \vec{q} = 0$
$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{r} = 1$, $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{r} = 0$

Expanding the given expression:
$(\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \cdot \vec{p} + (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) \cdot \vec{q} + (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) \cdot \vec{r}$

$= (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{p} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{p}) + (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{q} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{q}) + (\vec{c} \cdot \vec{r} + \vec{a} \cdot \vec{r})$

Substituting the values obtained above:
$= (1 + 0) + (1 + 0) + (1 + 0)$

$= 1 + 1 + 1 = 3$

Answer: $3$

question.text: If $|\bar{a}| = |\bar{b}| = 1, |\bar{c}| = 2$ and $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$, then the acute angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $\ldots$

solution.text:
Given $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

Using the vector triple product expansion:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a})\bar{c} + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

Since $|\bar{a}| = 1$, we have $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a} = 1$.

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} - \bar{c} + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

$\bar{b} = \bar{c} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a}$

Squaring both sides:

$|\bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{c}|^2 + (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2|\bar{a}|^2 - 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})$

Substituting $|\bar{a}| = 1$, $|\bar{b}| = 1$, and $|\bar{c}| = 2$:

$1 = 4 + (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2 - 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2$

$1 = 4 - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2$

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2 = 3$

Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{c}$. Then $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = |\bar{a}||\bar{c}|\cos\theta = 2\cos\theta$.

$(2\cos\theta)^2 = 3$

$4\cos^2\theta = 3 \Rightarrow \cos^2\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Since $\theta$ is an acute angle, $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

question.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are three non zero and non-coplanar vectors such that $\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = \dfrac{\bar{b}}{2}$, then the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is ...

solution.text:
Given $\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = \dfrac{\bar{b}}{2}$

Using the vector triple product expansion, we have:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c} = \dfrac{1}{2}\bar{b}$

Rearranging the terms, we get:

$\left(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c} = \bar{0}$

Since $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are non-coplanar vectors, $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ must be non-collinear. Therefore, their coefficients must be independently zero:

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} - \dfrac{1}{2} = 0 \Rightarrow \bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = 0$

Since $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are non-zero vectors, $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = 0$ implies that $\bar{a}$ is perpendicular to $\bar{b}$.

Thus, the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

question.text: Let $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ be three vectors having magnitudes 1, 1 and 2 respectively. If $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$, then the acute angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{c}$ is

solution.text:
Given $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

Using the vector triple product expansion:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a})\bar{c} + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

Since $|\bar{a}| = 1$, $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a} = 1$.

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} - \bar{c} + \bar{b} = \bar{0}$

$\bar{b} = \bar{c} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a}$

Squaring both sides:

$|\bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{c}|^2 + (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2 |\bar{a}|^2 - 2(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})$

$|\bar{b}|^2 = |\bar{c}|^2 - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})^2$

Substituting the given magnitudes $|\bar{a}| = 1$, $|\bar{b}| = 1$, and $|\bar{c}| = 2$:

$1^2 = 2^2 - (|\bar{a}||\bar{c}|\cos\theta)^2$

$1 = 4 - (1 \times 2 \times \cos\theta)^2$

$1 = 4 - 4\cos^2\theta$

$4\cos^2\theta = 3$

$\cos^2\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\cos\theta = \pm\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

For the acute angle, $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

question.text: If $\bar{a}, \overline{\mathrm{~b}}, \overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are three coplanar vectors such that $|\bar{a}|=1,|\overline{\mathrm{~b}}|=2, \overline{\mathrm{~b}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=8$ and the angle between $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $45^{\circ}$ then the value of $|\bar{a} \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})|$ is

solution.text:
Given $\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = 8$ and the angle between $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $45^{\circ}$.

$|\bar{b}| |\bar{c}| \cos 45^{\circ} = 8$

$2 |\bar{c}| \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 8 \Rightarrow |\bar{c}| = 4\sqrt{2}$

The magnitude of the cross product $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is:

$|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| = |\bar{b}| |\bar{c}| \sin 45^{\circ} = 2 \times 4\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 8$

Since $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are coplanar, the vector $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is perpendicular to the plane containing $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$, which means it is also perpendicular to $\bar{a}$.

Thus, the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is $90^{\circ}$.

$|\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})| = |\bar{a}| |\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| \sin 90^{\circ}$

$|\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})| = 1 \times 8 \times 1 = 8$

Answer: 8

question.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are three coplanar vectors such that $|\bar{a}|=1,|\bar{b}|=2$, $\overline{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=8$, the angle between $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $45^{\circ}$, then $|\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})|=$

solution.text:
Given $\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = 8$ and the angle between $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ is $45^{\circ}$.

$|\bar{b}| |\bar{c}| \cos 45^{\circ} = 8$

$2 |\bar{c}| \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 8$

$|\bar{c}| = 4\sqrt{2}$

The magnitude of the cross product of $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ is:

$|\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| = |\bar{b}| |\bar{c}| \sin 45^{\circ} = 2 \times 4\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 8$

Since $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are coplanar vectors, $\bar{a}$ lies in the plane containing $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$.

The vector $\bar{b} \times \bar{c}$ is perpendicular to the plane containing $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$, which means it is also perpendicular to $\bar{a}$. Thus, the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})$ is $90^{\circ}$.

Now, evaluating the magnitude of the vector triple product:

$|\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})| = |\bar{a}| |\bar{b} \times \bar{c}| \sin 90^{\circ}$

$|\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})| = 1 \times 8 \times 1 = 8$

Answer: 8

question.text: If $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are unit vectors and $|\bar{a}|=7$, $\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})+\bar{b} \times(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})=\frac{1}{2} \bar{a}$, then angle between the vectors $\bar{a}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ and angle between the vectors $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are respectively.

solution.text:
Given equation is $\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) + \vec{b} \times (\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) = \dfrac{1}{2} \vec{a}$

Using the vector triple product expansion, we have:

$(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})\vec{c} + (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a})\vec{c} - (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{a} = \dfrac{1}{2} \vec{a}$

Since $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}$, the terms involving $\vec{c}$ cancel out:

$(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{a} = \dfrac{1}{2} \vec{a}$

$(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{b} = \left( \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \dfrac{1}{2} \right) \vec{a}$

If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ were collinear, say $\vec{a} = k\vec{b}$, substituting this would give $k(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{b} = k\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\vec{b}$, which implies $k = 0$, contradicting $|\vec{a}| = 7$. Thus, $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are non-collinear vectors.

Equating the coefficients of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ to zero, we get:

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$

$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 0$

From $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$, the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $90^{\circ}$.

From $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$, and knowing $|\vec{b}| = 1$ and $|\vec{c}| = 1$, we have:

$|\vec{b}| |\vec{c}| \cos \theta = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\cos \theta = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = 120^{\circ}$

Therefore, the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $90^{\circ}$, and the angle between $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $120^{\circ}$.

Answer: $90^{\circ}, 120^{\circ}$

question.text: if $\bar{a}, \overline{\mathrm{~b}}, \overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are non coplanar unit vectors such that $\bar{a} \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})=\frac{\overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}}}{\sqrt{2}}$ Then the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ is

solution.text:
Using the vector triple product expansion:

$\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c}$

Given that:

$\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bar{b} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bar{c}$

Equating the coefficients of $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ (since $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are non-coplanar, $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ are non-collinear):

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$-(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$. Since $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are unit vectors, $|\bar{a}| = 1$ and $|\bar{b}| = 1$.

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = |\bar{a}||\bar{b}|\cos\theta = \cos\theta$

$\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

Answer: $\frac{3 \pi}{4}$

question.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { If } \bar{a}=4 \hat{i}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}, \quad \overline{\mathrm{b}}=\hat{i}-2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \text { then } \bar{a} \times(\bar{a} \times(\bar{a} \times(\bar{a} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})))=\end{aligned}$

solution.text:
Given $\bar{a} = 4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\bar{b} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

First, we find the dot products $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a}$ and $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}$:

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a} = |\bar{a}|^2 = (4)^2 + (3)^2 + (1)^2 = 16 + 9 + 1 = 26$

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = (4)(1) + (3)(-2) + (1)(2) = 4 - 6 + 2 = 0$

Using the vector triple product expansion, $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{a} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{a})\bar{b}$.

Substituting the values, we get:

$\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) = (0)\bar{a} - (26)\bar{b} = -26\bar{b}$

Now, we need to evaluate $\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{b})))$:

$\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}))) = \bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times (-26\bar{b}))$

$= -26 [\bar{a} \times (\bar{a} \times \bar{b})]$

$= -26 (-26\bar{b})$

$= 676\bar{b}$

Answer: $676 \overline{\mathrm{~b}}$

question.text: Let $\overline{\mathrm{a}}, \overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ be three non-zero vectors such that no two of them are collinear and $\left.(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{1}{3}|\overline{\mathrm{~b}}| \overline{\mathrm{c}} \right\rvert\, \overline{\mathrm{a}}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between vectors $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$, then the value of $\sin \theta$ is

solution.text:
Using the vector triple product formula:

$(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times \bar{c} = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a}$

Given that $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times \bar{c} = \dfrac{1}{3}|\bar{b}||\bar{c}|\bar{a}$, equating the two expressions gives:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} = \dfrac{1}{3}|\bar{b}||\bar{c}|\bar{a}$

Since $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are non-collinear vectors, their coefficients on both sides must be equal. Comparing the coefficients of $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$:

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = 0$

$-(\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c}) = \dfrac{1}{3}|\bar{b}||\bar{c}|$

Using the dot product formula $\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = |\bar{b}||\bar{c}|\cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$:

$-|\bar{b}||\bar{c}|\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{3}|\bar{b}||\bar{c}|$

$\cos \theta = -\dfrac{1}{3}$

Since $\theta$ is the angle between two vectors, $0 \le \theta \le \pi$, which means $\sin \theta \ge 0$.

$\sin \theta = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2 \theta} = \sqrt{1 - \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2}$

$\sin \theta = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{9}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{9}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$

Answer: $\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{3}$

question.text: Let $\overline{\mathrm{a}}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-2 \hat{k}$ and $\bar{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$. If $\bar{c}$ is a vector such that $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overline{\mathrm{c}}=|\overline{\mathrm{c}}|,|\overline{\mathrm{c}}-\overline{\mathrm{a}}|=2 \sqrt{2}$ and the angle between $(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ is $30^{\circ}$, then $|(\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}}) \times \overline{\mathrm{c}}|$ is equal to

solution.text:
Given $\overline{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$ and $\overline{b} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$.

The magnitude of $\overline{a}$ is:
$|\overline{a}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 1^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{9} = 3$

We are given $|\overline{c} - \overline{a}| = 2\sqrt{2}$. Squaring both sides, we get:
$|\overline{c}|^2 + |\overline{a}|^2 - 2(\overline{a} \cdot \overline{c}) = 8$

Substituting $|\overline{a}| = 3$ and the given condition $\overline{a} \cdot \overline{c} = |\overline{c}|$:
$|\overline{c}|^2 + 9 - 2|\overline{c}| = 8$

$|\overline{c}|^2 - 2|\overline{c}| + 1 = 0$

$(|\overline{c}| - 1)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow |\overline{c}| = 1$

Now, we find the cross product $\overline{a} \times \overline{b}$:
$\overline{a} \times \overline{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(0 - (-2)) - \hat{j}(0 - (-2)) + \hat{k}(2 - 1) = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$

The magnitude of $\overline{a} \times \overline{b}$ is:
$|\overline{a} \times \overline{b}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-2)^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{9} = 3$

The angle between $(\overline{a} \times \overline{b})$ and $\overline{c}$ is $30^{\circ}$. The magnitude of their cross product is:
$|(\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times \overline{c}| = |\overline{a} \times \overline{b}| |\overline{c}| \sin 30^{\circ}$

$|(\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times \overline{c}| = 3 \times 1 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Answer: $\frac{3}{2}$

question.text: If $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are non-coplanar unit vectors such that $\overline{\mathrm{a}} \times(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})=\frac{(\overline{\mathrm{b}}+\overline{\mathrm{c}})}{\sqrt{2}}$ then the angle between $\overline{\mathrm{a}}$ and $\bar{b}$ is

solution.text:
Using the vector triple product expansion:

$\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c}$

Given that:

$\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = \dfrac{\bar{b} + \bar{c}}{\sqrt{2}}$

Equating the two expressions:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bar{b} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bar{c}$

Since $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are non-coplanar, $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ are non-collinear. Equating the coefficients of $\bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ on both sides gives:

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$-(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Let $\theta$ be the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$. Since they are unit vectors, $|\bar{a}| = 1$ and $|\bar{b}| = 1$.

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = |\bar{a}||\bar{b}|\cos\theta = \cos\theta$

$\cos\theta = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

Answer: $\frac{3 \pi}{4}$

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

question.text: If $\overline{\mathrm{a}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}), \overline{\mathrm{b}}=\dfrac{1}{5}(\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}})$, then the value of $(2 \bar{a}-\bar{b}) \cdot\{(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times(\bar{a}+2 \bar{b})\}$ is

solution.text:
Given $\overline{a} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k})$ and $\overline{b} = \dfrac{1}{5}(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$.

First, we find the dot product $\overline{a} \cdot \overline{b}$:

$\overline{a} \cdot \overline{b} = \dfrac{1}{5\sqrt{10}} (4(1) - 3(2) + 1(2)) = \dfrac{1}{5\sqrt{10}} (4 - 6 + 2) = 0$

Next, simplify the vector triple product expression:

$\overline{v} = (\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times (\overline{a} + 2\overline{b}) = (\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times \overline{a} + 2(\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times \overline{b}$

Using the vector triple product expansion $(\overline{x} \times \overline{y}) \times \overline{z} = (\overline{x} \cdot \overline{z})\overline{y} - (\overline{y} \cdot \overline{z})\overline{x}$:

$(\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times \overline{a} = (\overline{a} \cdot \overline{a})\overline{b} - (\overline{b} \cdot \overline{a})\overline{a} = |\overline{a}|^2 \overline{b}$

$(\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times \overline{b} = (\overline{a} \cdot \overline{b})\overline{b} - (\overline{b} \cdot \overline{b})\overline{a} = -|\overline{b}|^2 \overline{a}$

Thus, $\overline{v} = |\overline{a}|^2 \overline{b} - 2|\overline{b}|^2 \overline{a}$.

Now, compute the dot product with $(2\overline{a} - \overline{b})$:

$(2\overline{a} - \overline{b}) \cdot \overline{v} = (2\overline{a} - \overline{b}) \cdot (|\overline{a}|^2 \overline{b} - 2|\overline{b}|^2 \overline{a})$

Expanding the dot product:

$= 2|\overline{a}|^2 (\overline{a} \cdot \overline{b}) - 4|\overline{a}|^2 |\overline{b}|^2 - |\overline{a}|^2 |\overline{b}|^2 + 2|\overline{b}|^2 (\overline{a} \cdot \overline{b})$

Since $\overline{a} \cdot \overline{b} = 0$, this reduces to:

$= -5|\overline{a}|^2 |\overline{b}|^2$

Assuming the intended vectors are unit vectors (as is standard when such typos occur in magnitudes in the problem statement), we have $|\overline{a}|^2 = 1$ and $|\overline{b}|^2 = 1$.

Therefore, the value is $-5(1)(1) = -5$.

Answer: -5

question.text: If $\overline{\mathrm{a}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $\bar{b}=\hat{i} \times(\bar{a} \times \hat{i})+\hat{j} \times(\bar{a} \times \hat{j})+\hat{k} \times(\bar{a} \times \hat{k})$ then $|\vec{b}|$ is

solution.text:
Using the vector triple product formula $\vec{x} \times (\vec{y} \times \vec{z}) = (\vec{x} \cdot \vec{z})\vec{y} - (\vec{x} \cdot \vec{y})\vec{z}$, we can expand each term in the expression for $\vec{b}$.

$\hat{i} \times (\vec{a} \times \hat{i}) = (\hat{i} \cdot \hat{i})\vec{a} - (\hat{i} \cdot \vec{a})\hat{i} = \vec{a} - a_1 \hat{i}$

$\hat{j} \times (\vec{a} \times \hat{j}) = (\hat{j} \cdot \hat{j})\vec{a} - (\hat{j} \cdot \vec{a})\hat{j} = \vec{a} - a_2 \hat{j}$

$\hat{k} \times (\vec{a} \times \hat{k}) = (\hat{k} \cdot \hat{k})\vec{a} - (\hat{k} \cdot \vec{a})\hat{k} = \vec{a} - a_3 \hat{k}$

Adding these three expressions gives:

$\vec{b} = 3\vec{a} - (a_1 \hat{i} + a_2 \hat{j} + a_3 \hat{k})$

Since $a_1 \hat{i} + a_2 \hat{j} + a_3 \hat{k} = \vec{a}$, we get:

$\vec{b} = 3\vec{a} - \vec{a} = 2\vec{a}$

Given $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, its magnitude is:

$|\vec{a}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 9} = \sqrt{14}$

Therefore, the magnitude of $\vec{b}$ is:

$|\vec{b}| = |2\vec{a}| = 2|\vec{a}| = 2\sqrt{14}$

Answer: $2 \sqrt{14}$

question.text: $\hat{a}, \hat{b}$, and $\hat{c}$ are three unit vectors such that $\hat{a} \times(\hat{b} \times \hat{c})=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(\hat{b}+\hat{c})$. If $\vec{b}$ is not parallel to $\hat{c}$, then the angle between $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ is
